title: Step sampling and terminal-step oversampling (p_terminal) in harnessed variants
question: For the step-by-step harnessed variants (cls, step_fork, step_ar, addressed_step_ar), how does sampling one column step k per generated problem (`all_steps=False`, giving `batch_size` independent `(alphabet, a, b)` problems per optimiser step) with terminal-step oversampling (`p_terminal = 0.2` vs. `0.0`) compare against yielding all `K + 1` steps of each problem sequentially (`all_steps=True`, where fixed `batch_size` sees only `~batch_size / E[K + 1]` distinct problems per optimiser step—`~18` at `batch_size=256` on `L=1..20`—with correlated consecutive rows and natural `1 / (K + 1)` terminal-flag frequency) in convergence per optimiser step, distinct problems seen, and `halt_accuracy`?
